ros2 launch course_bringup patrol.launch.py namespace:=robot_a subscriber_reliability:=best_effort record:=true bag_dir:=/tmp/pr05-all-queries-ready/bag

tests.name: 49 patrol tests and 10 course_bringup tests pass under pytest
Existing turtle_bringup copyright test is skipped by its original decorator
DDS relay preserves serialized Pose and delivers only to a compatible subscriber
Namespace and remap: course nodes under /robot_a, one global turtlesim, patrol output /turtle1/cmd_vel
record=false leaves no recorder or bag; record=true starts MCAP recorder through launch
Live reliable echo exits 124; subscriber count remains zero and RELIABILITY warning is logged
Live best_effort echo receives a pose and subscriber count increases
After stopping the live system, one player with QoS override feeds both profiles from the same bag
Replay reliable echo exits 124 and count stays zero; best_effort echo and node receive poses
MCAP SHA-256 is unchanged after both replay checks; launch processes finish cleanly

defect.reproducer: Launch with subscriber_reliability:=reliable record:=false. /robot_a/sensor_pose is visible; topic info shows a BEST_EFFORT publisher and RELIABLE subscriber. A 3-second reliable echo returns 124; the subscriber count stays zero. Repeat the reliable profile on the saved bag with best_effort playback: the same timeout and zero count occur. See qos-before.txt.
defect.root_cause: The sensor offers best_effort but the subscriber requests reliable. DDS discovers both endpoints but cannot match their reliability requirements, so no pose callbacks run.
defect.proof_after: Restart with subscriber_reliability:=best_effort record:=true. The live subscriber and echo receive poses. Stop the live launch and replay the same single MCAP with config/qos-overrides.yaml; best_effort receives while reliable still times out. Both checks use an unchanged bag SHA-256. See qos-after.txt and bag-metadata.yaml.
